etapes.texte: if + past: **would + verb**. if + had done: **would have done**
Formal English: __If I were you__, not if I was you

phrases.texte: These two types talk about situations that are not real. Type two is imaginary now: if plus past, then would.
Type three is imaginary in the past: if plus had done, then would have done.
Type two. If we had a bigger budget, we would hire more staff.
But we do not have a bigger budget now. It is only an idea.
Type three. If we had started earlier, we would have finished on time.
But we did not start earlier. It is a regret. It is too late.
Now, a TOEIC question. If she had known about the delay, she, blank, a taxi.
A: will take. B: would take. C: would have taken. D: had taken.
phrases.dit: Answer A. will take. Answer B. would take. Answer C. would have taken. Answer D. had taken.

phrases.texte: Read the if half first: if she had known. Had, plus a participle, means type three.
phrases.dit: Read the if half first: if she had known. Had, plus a participle, means type three.

phrases.texte: Will take is type one. Would take is type two. And D has no would.
phrases.dit: Will take, is type one. Would take, is type two. And D has no would.

phrases.texte: C is correct: if she had known about the delay, she would have taken a taxi.
Three steps. One: read the if half first.
Two: if plus past, would plus verb. If plus had done, would have done.
Three: in formal English, we say: if I were you.
